newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent spot market stable, paper softer.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent spot market stable, paper softer.

text.p: North Sea spot and paper crude oil markets were steady to firmer on Monday but trade was thin as buyers and sellers stood apart, traders said.
A cargo of May 4-6 Brent was bought by a trader at June Brent -37 cents for a minimum sized cargo while another trader picked up a May 6-8 cargo at a dated related price.

However, despite the firmer spot market June paper was traded slightly lower with $18.32 and $18.30 sold to two trade houses while $18.29 saw a refiner taking profit from the sale at $18.30. Paper spread play was very light with May/June seen done between two refiners at -20 cents.
Although there were no Brent cargoes on the original May Brent loading schedule for today, one cargo was brought forward early on Monday. This was kept by U.S. trade house Phibro.

While prices for other North Sea grades were also slightly firmer only Gulfaks C and Draugen barrels were traded. The former for May 10-12 dates at Dated Brent +10 cents and the latter for May 19-21 at Dated Brent +22 cents, some seven cents up from its previous trade.
"It's steady to firmer, the market doesn't seem to want to go down now. There are buyers around for most of the grades," one refiner said.

Brent CFDs for the next few weeks were roughly flat at 32 cents under June having been in contango for much of last week. This was due to gains of six cents for this week and four cent for the following two weeks.

Despite the flat market for weekly CFDs, monthly swaps against the front line IPE Brent futures remained in contango. Values were pegged around 32 cents under for May with June 24 cents under and July 20 cents under.
